verifications.reason: Heavily covered and the bullet's own centre of gravity. The Open Secure AI Alliance's declared scope is the whole agent stack — identity, permissions, isolation, guardrails, logs, model formats, multi-model scanning and secure coding workflows — built on the Linux Foundation's Akrites initiative and OpenSSF, with five security projects contributed at formation (NVIDIA's NOOA, Hugging Face's Safetensors, HPE's SPIFFE and SPIRE, IBM and Red Hat's Lightwell for signed patch distribution, Microsoft's MDASH). Agent identity, agent takeover and supply-chain integrity are all live in the rubric's generic-concept list.

NVIDIA convenes a thirty-seven-name Open Secure AI Alliance around the Hugging Face intrusion and contributes an open agent-governance framework, with OpenAI, Google and Anthropic absent from the roster
verifications.reason: Two genuine standing-out threads that exceed the enumerated rows they sit in. First, an open-weight licensing regime that gates commercial use by revenue rather than by field of use: a Model-as-a-Service operator whose revenue with affiliates passes 20 million dollars over any consecutive twelve months must sign a separate agreement before using the model at all, and any commercial product above 100 million monthly active users or 20 million dollars of monthly revenue must display Kimi K3 prominently in its interface, with internal use and access through Moonshot's own products or certified inference partners carved out — a licence-design story, not a model-release story. Second, industry-structure politics: a thirty-seven-name alliance whose roster reads as much by its absences (OpenAI, Google and Anthropic) as by its members, with NVIDIA arguing operationally rather than ideologically that defenders lose most when they cannot inspect, adapt and run advanced models on their own hardware.
